prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Document units:
S161: The Slot Coordinator is responsible for checking Calculated Takeoff Time feasibility and recording accepted slot adjustments, rejected slot adjustments, and unresolved slot conflicts in the Collaborative Decision Log.
S162: The Airport Duty Manager is responsible for maintaining the Airport Capacity Plan, declaring local operating impacts, and confirming transitions between Normal Operations, Adverse Weather Mode, Capacity Reduction State, and Recovery Phase.
S163: The Meteorology Briefing Officer uses the portal workspace to attach weather interpretation, forecast confidence, and expected timing of operational impacts without replacing the authoritative weather source.
S164: Cedarbell shall expose the current regional demand and constraint context to the shared workspace at each publication cycle without requiring manual re-entry.
S165: The Common Situation Display distinguishes values supplied by connected services, values confirmed by users, and values that have exceeded the configured freshness threshold.
S166: When a milestone becomes stale, the Airport CDM Portal shall highlight the affected flight and notify the role accountable for the next update through the Alert Distribution Hub.
S167: Each airport participant shall update a material change within two minutes of becoming aware of it during Normal Operations and within one minute during Adverse Weather Mode or Capacity Reduction State.
S168: If the exact value is not yet known, the accountable participant shall enter a provisional value with an uncertainty flag rather than leaving the milestone unchanged.
S169: The Collaborative Decision Log records who changed a value, when the change was made, whether the change was provisional or confirmed, and what operational decision relied on it.
S170: The Data Governance Steward defines the mandatory fields, permissible status values, retention rules, and data quality thresholds used by the Airport CDM Portal.
S171: The System Support Engineer monitors portal availability, interface latency, user session faults, and synchronization status against the Time Synchronization Service.
S172: During Contingency Fallback State, the Airport CDM Portal shall preserve the last synchronized milestone set and clearly mark any updates entered under degraded operating procedures.
S173: After operations, the Performance Analytics Warehouse uses the recorded milestones and decision history to compare planned outcomes with actual off-block, takeoff, landing, and stand events.
S174: Tower and airport duty coordination establishes the working link between live control positions, the airport duty desk, surface surveillance feeds, and operational safety checks.
S175: The Tower Supervisor remains accountable for control tower coordination and keeps the Airport Duty Manager informed of conditions that may affect runway, taxiway, stand, or apron availability.
S176: For this section only, Brindle is the operational alias used by Tower Supervisor during voice coordination drills.
S177: The Airport Duty Manager maintains the airport duty desk as the single operational point for airport status confirmation during Normal Operations, Adverse Weather Mode, Capacity Reduction State, and Recovery Phase.
S178: The duty desk reviews tower inputs, airport operations reports, and surveillance indications before confirming whether a local condition should be reflected in the Airport Capacity Plan.
S179: The Surface Surveillance Adapter consolidates position updates from the East Apron Sensor and West Apron Sensor and presents movement indications to the Airport CDM Portal.
S180: The Tower Sequence Manager uses validated surface status to support local sequencing decisions without replacing controller judgment or established radio procedures.
S181: The Airport Duty Manager uses the Runway Inspection Note to confirm that the duty desk has a current record of pavement status before endorsing any declared capacity change.
S182: Orchard shall issue time-stamped weather condition updates for use in tower and airport duty coordination.
S183: When surveillance data conflicts with tower observations, the Tower Supervisor and Airport Duty Manager agree on the operational interpretation before the condition is shared more widely.
S184: The Ramp Control Lead reviews apron movement constraints with the duty desk when stand access, pushback flow, or tug routing affects the departure plan.
S185: The Airport CDM Portal records duty desk confirmations as operational annotations linked to the relevant runway, taxiway, apron, or stand area.
S186: The Collaborative Decision Log captures the time, origin, and rationale for each local coordination decision that affects capacity or surface flow.
S187: The Time Synchronization Service shall keep tower, duty desk, surveillance, and portal event times aligned so that later review can reconstruct the sequence of events.
S188: Surface surveillance feeds are treated as advisory evidence for airport duty decisions unless the competent controller or airport authority confirms the operational effect.
S189: The Tower Supervisor verifies that any proposed reduction in declared runway use is consistent with observed traffic, controller workload, and the current safety position.
S190: The Airport Duty Manager verifies that airfield operations checks have been completed before requesting changes to Airport Acceptance Rate values or departure metering assumptions.
S191: The Regional Flow Platform receives confirmed capacity impacts through normal system interfaces after local duty coordination has established the airport position.
S192: The Capacity Assessment Module may use the confirmed airport position to recalculate available capacity, but it does not originate local airfield safety judgments.
